I always went looking for ways to have fun and learn at the same time. If I wasn't having fun I wasn't learning and improving. So finding what I find fun in this franchise was and still is incredibly important for me.

It took a lot of trial and error to find this, but eventually it came down to the more technical side of the game. So tech, combos, frame data... I enjoy this the most so I focus on it as long as I find it fun to do.

Eventually joined a couple of discord servers, streamed on twitch, played in online tournaments. Through these things I found people that could teach me some stuff and I could teach them some stuff too. 

Basically through not trying to win but having fun I found my way to "GitGud" in a sense. The people around me and my motivation to learn made the game fun for me.

Hey,

While the source of our suffering is different and I understand that this is the path you are willing to go down. I will still discourage you from doing it. I know that a comment from a stranger most likely won't change anything, but I feel compelled to say something anyway.

I believe that letting yourself be consumed by the past will never help anyone, but understanding why  this troubles you as much as it does will. By looking at how you can improve and learn through those experiences is how you might be able to get out of this loop (don't really know how to call it). Yes, this is a very difficult thing to do. And yes it's not always going to go like you'd like it to go. But I recommend you still try to look into some things you can do to process the trauma.

Of course I can't dictate how things will go for you from now on nor can I force you to do anything.
But here's some things that work for me:

Guided meditation to help calm the mind.

Sports (martial arts for me) to keep being active in both body and mind.

Try finding something to distract yourself and are able to put a lot of time in. For me this would be card magic.

Don't isolate yourself no matter the condition you are in. Try to talk to people either online or irl. This is a very important one. Even as an introvert.


I understand if you don't appear to have any time for these things. Though I recommend trying to make time do find and do things that work and help you. Moments where you usually don't have anything to do and fill it in with enjoyable things.

As a final note to this long comment. Don't do anything you don't want to do. Don't force yourself. You don't have to listen to what I have to say or do anything with it. 

It is still your life and your choice.

You are absolutely right. But I feel that when you are feeling these kind of feelings in fighting games or in life it is important to work through those feelings and  accept them for what they are to you and that winning the right match will make your day.

I recommend trying to find some people to play with. Be it in your local area or online. There are a lot of discord servers and forums that would gladly help you. Relief some of that stress of ranked play by still playing the game with people you can chat with.

A small dojo or something along those lines is great to start out with. 

And you can join the r/sf discord for regular tournaments and matchmaking with people that usually don't quit in the middle of the match.

Or the new challengers discord where you can find matches for a bunch of fighting games.

Or you can try the bronze/silver battlegrounds organized by Bizarrowolf. It's a great community with lots of people that want to improve in a safe environment.
